searchText: **protolambda** So.... The tests repo is taking surprisingly big amounts of bandwidth. Anyone not caching in CI? Otherwise we have to look at tests size again. Which would mean we either cut mainnet tests, or change some of the formats (but less dev friendly) Not neccesarily on ci but most likely locally. Is there a reason for LFS now that we have small files? They are split up, not smaller in total. Although subsequent changes are smaller LFS diffs now There are still files larger than 100gb? 100mb* <@203220829473996800> thanks for the reminder! I found we did misset our CI -> downloading 120MB per run... Fixed here: https://github.com/ethereum/trinity/pull/914. (It's still `v0.8.1` so we haven't split it into minimal and mainnet yet.) (It's not about Git LFS, we are using `tar.gz` release asserts) <adlerjohn> Offtopic: this might be a stupid question, but in [slash_validator](https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/v0.8.2/specs/core/0_beacon-chain.md#slash_validator) how are we guaranteed that the correct whistleblower is rewarded? Can't the block proposer just...pretend they're the whistleblower and get all the reward? the block proposer for slashings is always the whistleblower. In more long term games in phase 1 that span across multiple blocks, the whistleblower is remembered and gets a reward in addition to the block proposer the function was just made modular to be used in both cases Note that in both uses of `slash_validator` in phase one, no whistleblower is provided <adlerjohn> Oh I see. So for non-interactive proofs the proposer and whistleblower are the same, and for interactive proofs they may be different, basically? yes <adlerjohn> 👍 **cem_ozer** (in reply to **protolambda**) I disagree with this. In my opinion, if there was a deserialization spec for the latest spec version, it definitely would have sped up our catching up to the latest spec. **protolambda** @cem_ozer Noted, I will bring it up with the others **cem_ozer** Thank you

excerpts.author: eth2_bridge_bot
excerpts.content:
**protolambda**
So.... The tests repo is taking surprisingly big amounts of bandwidth. Anyone not caching in CI? Otherwise we have to look at tests size again. Which would mean we either cut mainnet tests, or change some of the formats (but less dev friendly)

excerpts.author: mpetrunic
excerpts.content: Not neccesarily on ci but most likely locally. Is there a reason for LFS now that we have small files?

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: They are split up, not smaller in total. Although subsequent changes are smaller LFS diffs now

excerpts.author: mpetrunic
excerpts.content: There are still files larger than 100gb?

excerpts.author: hsiaowei
excerpts.content:
<@203220829473996800>  thanks for the reminder! I found we did misset our CI -> downloading 120MB per run... Fixed here: https://github.com/ethereum/trinity/pull/914. (It's still `v0.8.1` so we haven't split it into minimal and mainnet yet.)

(It's not about Git LFS, we are using `tar.gz` release asserts)

excerpts.author: eth2_gitter_bot
excerpts.content: <adlerjohn> Offtopic: this might be a stupid question, but in [slash_validator](https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/v0.8.2/specs/core/0_beacon-chain.md#slash_validator) how are we guaranteed that the correct whistleblower is rewarded? Can't the block proposer just...pretend they're the whistleblower and get all the reward?

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: the block proposer for slashings is always the whistleblower. In more long term games in phase 1 that span across multiple blocks, the whistleblower is remembered and gets a reward in addition to the block proposer

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: the function was just made modular to be used in both cases

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: Note that in both uses of `slash_validator` in phase one, no whistleblower is provided

excerpts.author: eth2_gitter_bot
excerpts.content: <adlerjohn> Oh I see. So for non-interactive proofs the proposer and whistleblower are the same, and for interactive proofs they may be different, basically?

excerpts.author: eth2_bridge_bot
excerpts.content: I disagree with this. In my opinion, if there was a deserialization spec for the latest spec version, it definitely would have sped up our catching up to the latest spec.
